subject.title: The Skill Accumulation Problem: How many skills before your agent gets confused?

question: Should ClawHub add a first-class skill-governance surface for task-context recommendations and conflict/load-policy metadata, and how should it relate to the open capability-manifest RFC?
rationale: Current main only implements adjacent discovery and pinning pieces; the remaining behavior changes public metadata, privacy boundaries, and possibly OpenClaw runtime loading semantics.

options.title: Define the governance contract first
options.body: Write the recommendation inputs, conflict semantics, privacy boundary, and runtime/load-policy ownership in specs before implementing schema, API, UI, CLI, or OpenClaw changes.

options.title: Split capability metadata out
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/issues/2944 own declared trust-boundary metadata and keep this issue focused on recommender and accumulated-load-policy behavior.

options.title: Limit this to guidance
options.body: Keep product surfaces unchanged for now and answer with documented best practices for pruning, layering, and pinning skills.

recommendation.title: Define the governance contract first
recommendation.body: Write the recommendation inputs, conflict semantics, privacy boundary, and runtime/load-policy ownership in specs before implementing schema, API, UI, CLI, or OpenClaw changes.

likelyOwner.reason: This crosses CODEOWNERS-listed schema, API, CLI, and security-adjacent metadata surfaces where Patrick-Erichsen is the strongest current routing signal.
